meta.title: Synthetic fixture — offline collaboration research atlas
meta.updated: fixture day 4 (not an actual research date)
meta.goal: Synthetic teaching example: explore offline-first collaborative editing mechanisms for maintainers of shared workspace software. No real research, sources, experiments, or audience endorsement are represented.
meta.standing: All rounds, scores, source labels, and reviewer roles are simulated. No actual independent evaluation occurred; no proposal passes. Four areas retain three unsearched routes and two active investigations.
meta.standard: Illustrative configured sections: Novelty 94, Impressiveness 94, Feasibility 80, Evidence quality 80. Potential mode, not measured success. All sections and hard constraints must pass. Best means highest total across comparable scored sections, display only, never another gate. Rubric, audience, mode, and constraints stay fixed here; changes would make comparisons unsuitable. Sources are fictional no-link labels.
meta.pass_rule: all sections >= threshold and no hard constraint violated
meta.what_worked: Within the synthetic scenario, separating merge correctness, permission authority, recovery cost, and user agency exposed genuinely different next questions.
glossary: Invented fixture content, not a research finding or real source.

blockers.text: This fixture contains invented summaries only, not actual evaluation-roundN.json reports. The simulated separate-reviewer role is a teaching device; it establishes neither independent research nor approval.

risks.title: Synthetic sources are not evidence
risks.text: SIM-S1–SIM-S8 are invented no-link labels, not real citations or claims about existing software.
risks.check: Replace the entire scenario with actual located primary sources and receipts before using it for a real decision.

risks.title: Constraints can disappear in a pivot
risks.text: Weakening offline revocation to expiry changes the guarantee; a useful fallback cannot silently become the original promise.
risks.check: Keep the original constraint visible and obtain any required user authorization before changing it.

risks.title: Two high sections are not a pass
risks.text: R7's synthetic Novelty 96 and Impressiveness 95 exceed 94, but Feasibility 62 fails 80; Evidence quality is 85/80. Its highest total is display-only.
risks.check: Require every configured section and every hard constraint using the actual report and mode-appropriate evidence; never promote an atlas summary into approval.

results.text: Synthetic scores: Novelty 96, Impressiveness 95, Feasibility 62, Evidence quality 85. Isolate cascading dependencies; passing the first two sections cannot hide failed Feasibility.

lessons.pattern: Domain changes can hide identical machinery.
lessons.evidence: Synthetic R1/SIM-S1 and R5/SIM-S5 close two repackaged mechanisms.
lessons.check: State the guarantee remaining after the strongest baseline, with a distinguishing trace.

lessons.pattern: Partition claims need an information premise.
lessons.evidence: Synthetic R3/SIM-S3 defeats instantaneous revocation without a new local observation.
lessons.check: Write two indistinguishable local histories before claiming a remote event is known.

lessons.pattern: Explanation polish is not yet an explanation contribution.
lessons.evidence: Synthetic R6: Novelty 90, Impressiveness 87, Feasibility 78, Evidence quality 77; SIM-S6 already previews operations. R9 relabels SIM-S8.
lessons.check: Specify the user's decision and a different observable guarantee, not renamed controls.

lessons.pattern: High novelty and appeal cannot compensate for failed feasibility.
lessons.evidence: Synthetic R7: Novelty 96, Impressiveness 95, Feasibility 62, Evidence quality 85 against thresholds 94/94/80/80.
lessons.check: Check all configured sections and all hard constraints independently; challenge the dependency-summary premise.

calibration_notes: Every estimate and reviewer score is invented for this synthetic fixture. Separate builder/reviewer roles model the desired comparison, not actual independent agents or source checks.

In a real loop compare timestamped pre-review predictions with independently researched scores. If agents are unavailable, explicitly disclose sequential mode and keep it separate from independent calibration.
Cross-angle error examples do not show that revisions improved one proposal, predict acceptance, or measure practical benefit. R3 and R9 were builder discards without scores.
